analysis:
Examined the changed regions of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (head lines ~714-724, 747-749, 975-976, 1106-1108). The media path now computes a reasoningPrefix up front, from the rendered media prompt tokens or the content seed. It passes that to the new stopStringScope argument of bridge.submitTokenized and reuses it in makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream. Previously the prefix was computed later, after the submit (base lines ~750-761). Text path gains stopStringScope at head lines 975-976 in the same way. The hunk at 1106-1108 is outside the supplied excerpt, so it was not examined.

Security view: this is parser and stop-string state initialization, with no new trust boundary, no new data egress, and no change to cache scope, cacheSalt, encryption, attestation, or authorization. Cache plumbing is unchanged (cacheScope: requestCacheScope, cacheEnabled, hybridPrefixIdentity), so T-041 mitigations are untouched. Error paths still release reservations: any throw inside the do block reaches the catch that calls mediaGate.release and releaseBox.fire. The new streamingPrefix and decode calls are synchronous, bounded to a tail decode, and sit between existing checkFirstContentDeadline calls. The prompt-token decode happens only in provider memory and is not logged or transmitted.

Residual integration questions, outside the supplied evidence: the bridge's submitTokenized signature and the ReasoningStopScope behavior. A wrong scope could cause stop strings to be applied in the reasoning channel or to be missed, which is a correctness or output-shaping concern rather than confidentiality. The remaining 1106-1108 hunk and the patch tail were also not visible.
